Notes

一个feat要一个比特币

The English abbreviation feat is used inside the Chinese sentence for a guest feature. The lyric quotes a price of one bitcoin; it is a boast in the text, not a verified booking rate.

  • Genius community transcript
没有戏

没有戏 literally says there is no play or performance; colloquially it means something has no prospect of working out. Here it dismisses the other person’s chances immediately after pricing a feature. It need not mean that a literal stage role has been refused.

  • Lyric text
山顶洞人

山顶洞人 is the Chinese name for the prehistoric humans associated with the Upper Cave at Zhoukoudian, near Beijing. In this taunt, that recognizable name is compressed into “caveman,” then coupled with ritual dancing. The historical term supplies the image; the verse is not describing an archaeological practice.

  • Chinese Academy of Sciences: Zhoukoudian Upper Cave research
  • Lyric text
套路

套路 can mean an organized set of moves and, colloquially, a predictable maneuver or manipulative ploy. After the wriggling, silk-spitting spectacle fails to affect him, the speaker asks for simpler 套路. The word makes the display sound rehearsed rather than powerful.

  • Lyric text
素三鲜还是地三鲜

三鲜 means “three delicacies.” 地三鲜 is the familiar combination of eggplant, potato, and green pepper; 素三鲜 means a vegetarian trio, with the exact ingredients left unspecified here. After intimidation and the bitcoin feature price, the choice is suddenly an ordinary meal, followed by turning the serving tray and letting others eat first.

  • CCTV 天天饮食: 地三鲜 ingredients and preparation
  • Lyric text
正道的光

This phrase also appears in Huang Bo’s song 正义之道, “The Way of Justice,” documented in CCTV’s performance archive. Here it is repeated beside the black-and-white taiji image and the title “Lord Kai,” lending the chant the vocabulary of righteousness. The textual echo does not by itself establish use of an audio sample.

  • CCTV: Huang Bo performs 正义之道
  • 正义之道 lyric text
  • Lyric text
一黑一白太极

太极 is not limited to the martial art called tai chi in English. The explicit black and white also evoke the taiji diagram, a circle of interlocking yin and yang halves. That gives the line a compact visual emblem rather than necessarily describing someone doing exercises.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 太極圖
  • Lyric text
凯神

凯神 combines Kai with 神, “god” or a godlike master. “Lord Kai” keeps the self-mythologizing form without treating it as a literal claim of divinity.

  • Genius community transcript
